correctness.rationale: The continuous stationary density proportional to (sigma^2+b^2 x^2)^(-1-a/b^2) has density tail |x|^(-2-2/r), so its fourth moment is finite exactly for r<2/3. The drift-only midpoint update is the random affine recurrence Y_next=A Y+C with independent Gaussian coefficients, E[A^2]<1 for 0<r<2, so its unique stationary law exists in L² and has variance s/(2-r). Its fourth moment is finite iff E[A^4]<1: sufficiency by L4 convergence of the affine series, necessity from the strictly positive fourth-moment fixed-point numerator. Direct Gaussian expansion gives 1-E[A^4]=4t[(2-3r)(1+t²)+3r(2-r)t]/(1+t)^4; an AM–GM argument yields the exact trichotomy and equality boundaries. The displayed moment formula and strict physical comparison follow algebraically. Standard-library exact-rational replay: 3028 assertions; finite tests support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Numerical stationary covariance is often used to gauge invariant-measure fidelity. The new all-step phase diagram shows a qualitatively important failure of covariance exactness for tail-sensitive quantities: a discretization can possess a finite fourth moment even when the true equilibrium has none, and its fourth moment is strictly biased low whenever the physical fourth moment exists. The reciprocal nonmonotone finite-moment interval supplies an exact benchmark for step choice and stochastic theta integrator analysis; this is not merely second-moment restatement.
